title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (November 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET — the edition that restates October
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, re-read this session off conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-11-30 is the last Tuesday of November 2027. CORROBORATED FOR NOVEMBER SPECIFICALLY, 3 of 3 and every one double-sourced, FROM EDITIONS THIS CHAIN HAD NEVER REACHED BEFORE THIS SESSION: CCI-Nov-2022 (888,059 bytes, Updated 2022-11-29), CCI-Nov-2023 (1,041,462 bytes, Updated 2023-11-28), CCI-Nov-2024 (890,772 bytes, Updated 2024-11-26), each fetched direct 2026-09-06 serially and each verified against its own Updated stamp rather than trusted by slug. Each is the last Tuesday of its November, and each was ANNOUNCED IN ADVANCE by its own October predecessor's next-release line, also read this session: CCI-Oct-2022 "The next release is Tuesday, November 29", CCI-Oct-2023 "Tuesday, November 28", CCI-Oct-2024 "Tuesday, November 26th". THE SLUG CONVENTION FOR NOVEMBER IS ABBREVIATED-ONLY IN ALL THREE YEARS -- CCI-November-2022, CCI-November-2023 and CCI-November-2024 each redirect to the 332,031-byte topic landing page -- which is a fresh instance of the 09-28 sibling's finding that the convention is per-month-per-year and must be probed, not derived. INDEPENDENTLY DATED BY A SECOND PUBLISHER: fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-06) posts a "2027 HPI Release Dates" table whose eleventh row reads "Tuesday, November 30 | Quarterly Index (with Monthly Tables) | September 2027 and 2027Q3" -- one of twelve 2027 rows, all twelve matching this chain's rule-derived last Tuesdays. That corroborates the calendar arithmetic, not the Conference Board's intentions. No November-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a newly verified November record. notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-10-26 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), one edition forward on the same chain. PROPOSED FOR A SPECIFIC REASON, NOT BECAUSE THE CHAIN SHOULD KEEP ROLLING: the November edition is the document that scores this session's single most usable finding. OCTOBER'S FIRST PRINT IS THE LEAST TRUSTWORTHY IN THIS CHAIN, and it is the November edition that proves it. The three November editions restate their October predecessors -0.3 / -3.5 / +0.9 on the headline -- 1 of 3 up, mean -0.97 -- and the -3.5 (October 2023's 102.6 restated to a "downwardly revised 99.1") is the largest downward headline revision anywhere in this chain, past the previous record of -3.0. The November 2027 edition restates October 2027, so it is the document that tests the rule rather than argues it. FOUR CAUTIONS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS. (1) NOVEMBER IS A CLEAN PRINT, NOT A COLLISION. The 2027 FOMC panel has no November meeting at all (October 26-27 then December 7-8), so 2027-11-30 is the opposite configuration to the October print this proposal comes from -- do not carry October's collision framing into it. (2) NOVEMBER'S CUT-OFF LAGS ARE THE LONGEST AND WIDEST IN THE CHAIN, AND THEY ARE ALREADY SOURCED 3 OF 3 -- do not borrow October's. All three editions state one: CCI-Nov-2022 "the cutoff date for the preliminary results was November 18" against a 11-29 release (11 days), CCI-Nov-2023 "...was November 15" against 11-28 (13 days), CCI-Nov-2024 "...was November 18, 2024" against 11-26 (8 days). That is a 5-day spread on lags of 8 to 13, against October's 6/7/6 and September's 7/8/7 -- the widest and longest anywhere in this chain, and the obvious mechanism is Thanksgiving sitting inside the field window. For 2027 (Thanksgiving 2027-11-25, release 2027-11-30) the honest projection is a cut-off somewhere in 11-17 to 11-22 with real uncertainty, not a point estimate. (3) THE MONTH'S CELL IS QUIET, NOT WIDE. VIX medians run Sep 17.17, OCT 19.33, Nov 17.21 -- November gives back essentially all of October's widening, so a reader arriving from the October ledger should expect the regime to reverse, not persist. (4) DO NOT RE-FETCH THE PUBLISHER CONCURRENTLY: the 09-28 sibling tripped its origin's captcha (HTTP 200 serving a 1,021-byte "User validation required" page, error code 421) by issuing parallel requests. This session made 22 serial fetches and hit it zero times, which confirms the rule rather than tests it; a byte-count check remains the only thing that catches a captcha page. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
